doc.title: Sheila Jordan — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Bird-and-Fats medley with Bird's intro to Scrapple
summary: They build medleys like the dance songs and a Bird and Fats Waller medley, with Cameron's idea of using Bird's Scrapple intro under Honeysuckle Rose.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Oh, yeah, yeah. Yeah, we do. We have, we… I, well, these… some of these I had arranged with Harvey but what Cameron and I have done now is stretched them out even further. Added on to them. So as I said, we have the dance medley with all songs about dancing. Fred Astaire and Ginger Rogers, you know. And then we have the Bird… a Bird, uh, and Fats medley. Brown, C.: Well, Fats and Bird, I think, I think I sorta contributed the idea of using…

Right. You did. Brown, C.: …to scrapple underneath the head of Honeysuckle where it sorta doesn‟t really fit. But of course, Sheila‟s ears are so good, she could sing the melody through the little dissonance of that. Just a little, you know.
Brown, C.: And then finally we come back to scrapple. So we‟re trying to, you know, do some… what do they call that? Uh, deceptive cadences. And then tie it all together in the…
